questions.question: Why are megaphones, loudhailers and some musical instruments designed with a tube followed by a conical opening?

options.text: To direct most of the sound waves forward toward the audience without spreading it
To spread the sound in all directions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To direct most of the sound waves forward toward the audience without spreading it**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Megaphones**, **loudhailers**, and instruments like **trumpets** and **shehnais** are designed based on the principle of **multiple reflection of sound**.
 
• The **tube** followed by a **conical opening** acts as a guide that reflects **sound waves** multiple times within the internal walls of the device.
 
• This specific **conical shape** ensures that the **sound waves** do not spread out in all directions but are instead focused and **directed forward** toward the intended audience. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• By preventing the **spherical spreading** of sound energy, these devices maintain a higher **intensity** of sound over a **greater distance**.
 
• The **amplitude** of the sound waves in the forward direction is effectively increased because the energy is concentrated in a **narrower beam**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reflection of Sound:**

 
 
• Similar to light, **sound waves** follow the laws of **reflection**, where the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection.
 
• In a **megaphone**, the successive reflections within the **conical flare** allow the sound to exit with a more uniform **phase** and **direction**.
 
 
 
• **Acoustic Impedance Matching:**
 
 
• The **conical opening** serves as an **acoustic transformer**. It helps in matching the high **acoustic impedance** of the narrow tube to the low **acoustic impedance** of the open air.
 
• This matching allows for a more efficient transfer of **sound energy** from the source to the atmosphere, making the instrument or device **louder**.
 
 
 
• **Musical Instruments:**
 
 
• Instruments like the **trombone**, **tuba**, and **French horn** use a flared "bell" at the end to project sound.
 
• The size and **curvature** of the **conical flare** determine the **timbre** and **directional characteristics** of the musical notes produced.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• **Megaphones** are widely used by **coaches**, **police officers**, and **protest leaders** to amplify voices without electronic assistance.
 
• The **design** is purely **mechanical**, relying on the physics of **geometry** and **acoustics** to enhance communication in open spaces.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inverse Square Law:** Normally, **sound intensity** decreases inversely with the square of the **distance** from the source. However, by using a **conical opening**, this energy loss is mitigated in a specific **direction**.
 
• **Speed of Sound:** It is important to note that while the **direction** and **intensity** are altered, the **speed of sound** (approx. **343 meters per second** in air at **20 degrees Celsius**) remains constant.
 
• **Frequency and Wavelength:** The **design** of the cone is often optimized for human **vocal frequencies** (roughly **300 Hz to 3400 Hz**) to ensure maximum **clarity** and **intelligibility**.

questions.question: An atom has 11 protons, 11 electrons and 12 neutrons. What is the mass number of that atom?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23**__.

• **The mass number** of an atom is the total number of **protons** and **neutrons** in its nucleus. It is calculated using the formula:

 **Mass Number = Number of Protons + Number of Neutrons**.
 
• In the given question, the atom has **11 protons** and **12 neutrons**. Substituting these values into the formula:

 **Mass Number = 11 + 12 = 23**.
 
• Electrons are not included in the calculation of the mass number because their mass is negligible compared to protons and neutrons.
 
• The given atom has **11 electrons**, which balances the 11 protons, ensuring the atom is electrical

questions.question: Which gas reacts with sodium hydroxide to form sodium bicarbonate and sodium carbonate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CO2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)** is an **acidic oxide** that reacts readily with **strong bases** like **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)** to form different salts based on the concentration of the gas.
 
• When **CO₂** is passed through a solution of **Sodium Hydroxide**, it first reacts to form **Sodium Carbonate (Na₂CO₃)** and **water (H₂O)**. The chemical equation for this reaction is **2NaOH + CO₂ → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• If **Carbon Dioxide** is provided in **excess**, it continues to react with the **Sodium Carbonate** and **water** formed in the first step to produce **Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO₃)**, also known as **Sodium Hydrogen Carbonate**. The equation for this subsequent step is **Na₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ → 2NaHCO₃**.
 
• This process is a classic example of a **neutralization reaction** between an **acidic gas** and an **alkali**. It is industrially significant as it relates to the absorption of greenhouse gases and the production of chemical reagents.
 
• Other gases listed do not yield these specific products. **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO₂)** is an acidic gas that reacts with **NaOH** to produce **Sodium Nitrate (NaNO₃)** and **Sodium Nitrite (NaNO₂)**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **Carbon Monoxide (CO)** is considered a **neutral oxide** and does not react with **Sodium Hydroxide** under standard temperature and pressure conditions. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Sulfur Dioxide (SO₂)** reacts with **NaOH** to form **Sodium Sulfite (Na₂SO₃)** and **Sodium Bisulfite (NaHSO₃)**, following a similar pattern but producing sulfur-based salts instead of carbonates. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH):**

 
 
• Commonly known as **Caustic Soda**, it is a highly **alkaline** white solid.
 
• It is widely used in the manufacture of **pulp and paper**, **textiles**, **drinking water**, **soaps**, and **detergents**.
 
• In the **year 2022**, the global production of **NaOH** reached millions of metric tons due to its versatile chemical **functions** as a strong base.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Carbonate (Na₂CO₃):**
 
 
• Commonly referred to as **Washing Soda**, it is the **disodium salt** of carbonic acid.
 
• It is primarily used in **glass manufacturing**, where it acts as a **flux** to lower the melting point of silica.
 
• It also finds **applications** in **water softening** by removing temporary and permanent hardness.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Bicarbonate (NaHCO₃):**
 
 
• Commonly known as **Baking Soda**, it is a white crystalline solid with a slightly **alkaline** taste.
 
• It is used in **cooking** as a leavening agent and in **fire extinguishers** because it releases **CO₂** when heated, which helps smother flames.
 
• In the medical field, it is used as an **antacid** to treat **acid indigestion** and **heartburn**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental and Industrial Context:**
 
 
• The reaction between **NaOH** and **CO₂** is utilized in **Carbon Capture and Storage (CCS)** technologies to scrub **Carbon Dioxide** from industrial exhaust streams.
 
• This chemical interaction is fundamental in the **Solvay Process**, which is the major industrial process for the production of **Sodium Carbonate** globally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Oxide Classification:** **CO₂** and **SO₂** are **Non-metallic oxides**, which are generally **acidic** in nature. In contrast, **CO** and **N₂O** are rare examples of **neutral** non-metallic oxides.
 
• **Detection of CO₂:** The reaction of **CO₂** with **Calcium Hydroxide [Ca(OH)₂]**, also known as **Lime Water**, is the standard laboratory test for the gas. It turns lime water **milky** due to the formation of insoluble **Calcium Carbonate**, but becomes clear again if **excess CO₂** is passed through (forming soluble Calcium Bicarbonate).
 
• **Stoichiometry:** The ratio of **NaOH** to **CO₂** determines the product. A **2:1 molar ratio** favors the **carbonate**, while a **1:1 molar ratio** (or excess gas) favors the **bicarbonate**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a saturated hydrocarbon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Propane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saturated hydrocarbons** are organic compounds where the **carbon atoms** are connected to each other only by **single bonds**. These are also known as **alkanes**.
 
• **Propane** is an **alkane** with the chemical formula **C3H8**. Since it contains only single covalent bonds between its three **carbon atoms**, it is classified as a **saturated hydrocarbon**. ***Hence, this option is correct.***
 
• **Ethene** (C2H4) belongs to the group of **alkenes**, which are **unsaturated hydrocarbons** containing at least one **double bond** between carbon atoms. ***Hence, this option is incorrect.***
 
• **Ethyne** (C2H2) and **Butyne** (C4H6) belong to the group of **alkynes**. These are **unsaturated hydrocarbons** containing at least one **triple bond** between carbon atoms. ***Hence, these options are incorrect.***
 
• The general formula for **saturated hydrocarbons** (alkanes) is **CnH2n+2**, where **n** represents the **number of carbon atoms** in the molecule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification of Hydrocarbons:**

 
 
• **Alkanes:** These are **saturated** compounds with the general formula **CnH2n+2**. Common examples include **Methane (CH4)**, **Ethane (C2H6)**, and **Butane (C4H10)**. They are primarily used as **fuels** (e.g., LPG consists mostly of propane and butane).
 
• **Alkenes:** These are **unsaturated** compounds featuring at least one **double bond** with the formula **CnH2n**. **Ethene** is the simplest alkene, often used in the production of **plastics** like **polyethylene**.
 
• **Alkynes:** These are **unsaturated** compounds featuring at least one **triple bond** with the formula **CnH2n-2**. **Ethyne**, commonly known as **acetylene**, is used in **welding torches**.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Reactivity:**
 
 
• **Saturated hydrocarbons** are relatively **unreactive** under normal conditions and are often referred to as **paraffins** (meaning "little affinity"). They undergo **substitution reactions**.
 
• **Unsaturated hydrocarbons** are more **chemically reactive** because of the presence of double or triple bonds, which can easily break to form new bonds in **addition reactions**.
 
 
 
• **Structure and Hybridization:**
 
 
• In **alkanes** (saturated), carbon atoms are **sp3 hybridized**, leading to a **tetrahedral geometry**.
 
• In **alkenes**, the double-bonded carbons are **sp2 hybridized**, while in **alkynes**, the triple-bonded carbons are **sp hybridized**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nomenclature Prefixes:** The names of hydrocarbons are based on the **number of carbon atoms**: 1 (**meth-**), 2 (**eth-**), 3 (**prop-**), 4 (**but-**), 5 (**pent-**), etc.
 
• **Physical State:** The first four **alkanes** (C1 to C4) are **gases** at room temperature, while those with 5 to 17 carbons are **liquids**, and those with 18 or more carbons are **solids**.
 
• **Combustion:** All **hydrocarbons** burn in the presence of **oxygen** to produce **carbon dioxide**, **water**, and **heat energy**, making them excellent **energy sources**.

questions.question: During uniform motion of an object along a straight line __________.

options.text: The change in velocity over any time interval is zero.
The change in velocity over any time interval is non zero.
The velocity has different values at different instants and at different points of the path.
The velocity changes continuously with time.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The change in velocity over any time interval is zero**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uniform Motion** is defined as the motion of an object in which the object travels in a **straight line** and covers **equal distances** in **equal intervals of time**, regardless of the duration of the time interval.
 
• In this type of motion, the **magnitude** of the **velocity** (speed) and the **direction** of motion remain **constant** throughout the entire duration of the journey.
 
• The **change in velocity** (represented as Δv) is calculated by subtracting the initial velocity from the final velocity. Since the velocity is constant at every **instant** of time in uniform motion, the difference is always **zero**. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• If the change in velocity over any time interval were **non-zero**, it would imply that the object is either speeding up or slowing down, which characterizes **non-uniform** or **accelerated motion**. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• During uniform motion, the **velocity** remains the **same** at all **instants** and at all **points** along the path; it does not fluctuate. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*
 
• A velocity that **changes continuously** with **time** indicates that the object is undergoing **acceleration** (or deceleration), which contradicts the fundamental definition of uniform motion. *Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Velocity and Speed:** In the context of **straight-line motion** without a change in direction, the **magnitude** of **velocity** is equal to the **speed** of the object. Velocity is a **vector quantity**, meaning it accounts for both speed and direction.
 
• **Acceleration in Uniform Motion:** **Acceleration** is the rate of change of velocity with respect to time. Since the velocity is **constant** in uniform motion, the **acceleration** is always **zero**.
 
• **Graphical Representation:**
 
 
• In a **Distance-Time Graph**, uniform motion is represented by a **straight line** with a constant **slope**, indicating that distance is **directly proportional** to time.
 
• In a **Velocity-Time Graph**, uniform motion is represented by a **horizontal straight line** parallel to the **time axis** (x-axis), showing that velocity does not change as time progresses.
 
 
 
• **Mathematical Formula:** For an object in uniform motion, the **distance** (s) covered is the product of **velocity** (v) and **time** (t), expressed as **s = v × t**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Directional Constraint:** For motion to remain **uniform** along a **straight line**, the object must not turn back. If the object reverses direction, even at the same speed, the **velocity** changes because the **direction vector** changes.
 
• **Instantaneous vs. Average:** In **uniform motion**, the **instantaneous velocity** (velocity at a specific moment) is always equal to the **average velocity** (total displacement divided by total time) because the rate of motion is **steady**.
 
• **Examples:** A **light wave** traveling through a **vacuum** moves in uniform motion at a constant speed of approximately **3 × 10⁸ meters per second**. Similarly, a car set on **cruise control** driving on a perfectly straight **highway** approximates uniform motion.
 
• **Non-Uniform Motion:** Most real-world movements are **non-uniform**, where objects cover **unequal distances** in equal intervals of time due to **friction**, **traffic**, or **external forces**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a property of ionic compounds?

options.text: They generally have high melting and boiling points.
They are generally solid at room temperature.
They can conduct electricity in an aqueous/molten state.
They are soluble in solvents such as kerosene and petrol.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They are soluble in solvents such as kerosene and petrol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Melting and Boiling Points**: Ionic compounds possess **high melting and boiling points**. This is due to the presence of a very strong **electrostatic force of attraction** between the **positively charged ions (cations)** and **negatively charged ions (anions)**, which requires a significant amount of **thermal energy** to overcome. ***Hence, statement 1 is a correct property.***
 
• **Physical Nature**: These compounds are **solids** and are somewhat **hard** at **room temperature** because of the strong force of attraction between the ions. They are generally **brittle** and tend to break into pieces when **pressure** is applied. ***Hence, statement 2 is a correct property.***
 
• **Electrical Conductivity**: The conduction of electricity through a solution involves the movement of **charged particles**. Ionic compounds **conduct electricity** in the **molten state** or when dissolved in **water (aqueous solution)** because the ions become free to move. However, they do **not conduct electricity** in the **solid state** because the movement of ions is restricted by the rigid **crystal structure**. ***Hence, statement 3 is a correct property.***
 
• **Solubility**: Electrovalent or ionic compounds are generally **soluble in water** (which is a **polar solvent**) but are **insoluble** in organic solvents such as **kerosene, petrol, benzene, and ether** (which are **non-polar solvents**). This follows the principle of **"like dissolves like."** ***Hence, statement 4 is NOT a property of ionic compounds.***
 
• ***Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Formation of Ionic Bonds**: An **ionic bond** is formed by the **complete transfer** of one or more **valence electrons** from a **metal atom** to a **non-metal atom**. This transfer results in the formation of **ions** that achieve a stable **noble gas electronic configuration**.
 
• **Lattice Energy**: The stability of an ionic compound is attributed to its **lattice energy**, which is the energy released when one mole of an ionic crystalline compound is formed from **gaseous ions**. **Magnesium Oxide (MgO)** and **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)** are classic examples of such structures.
 
• **Crystal Lattice**: Ionic compounds do not exist as single molecules but as **aggregates** of ions arranged in a regular **three-dimensional** pattern called a **crystal lattice**. For instance, in **NaCl**, each **Sodium ion** is surrounded by six **Chloride ions** and vice-versa.
 
• **Comparison with Covalent Compounds**: Unlike ionic compounds, **covalent compounds** are formed by the **sharing of electrons**. They generally have **lower melting and boiling points**, can be **gases, liquids, or solids** at room temperature, and are typically **non-conductors** of electricity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dielectric Constant**: Water has a high **dielectric constant** (approx. **80**), which weakens the **electrostatic forces** between ions, facilitating their **dissociation** and making water an excellent solvent for ionic substances.
 
• **Hydration Energy**: When an ionic compound dissolves in water, the ions are surrounded by water molecules, a process called **hydration**. If the **hydration energy** is higher than the **lattice energy**, the compound will be **soluble**.
 
• **Chemical Reactivity**: Reactions involving ionic compounds in **aqueous solutions** are usually very **fast** because they occur between **free ions** rather than neutral atoms or molecules.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about resistivity is correct?

options.text: It depends only on the nature and temperature of the material
It increases with the cross-sectional area
It changes with the shape of the conductor
It decreases when the length increases

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It depends only on the nature and temperature of the material**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Resistivity**, also known as **specific electrical resistance**, is an intrinsic property of a material that quantifies how strongly it opposes the flow of electric current.
 
• The **resistivity** of a material depends only on the **nature of the material** and its **temperature**. It does not depend on the physical dimensions such as **length** or **cross-sectional area**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **resistance (R)** of a conductor is proportional to its **length (L)** and inversely proportional to its **cross-sectional area (A)**, expressed as **R = ρ (L/A)**, where **ρ (rho)** is the **resistivity**. While resistance changes with area, the **resistivity** constant remains the same for a specific material at a constant temperature. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Since **resistivity** is a material constant, it does not change with the **shape** or **size** of the conductor. Whether the material is shaped into a thin wire or a thick block, its **resistivity** remains identical. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• **Resistivity** is independent of the **length** of the conductor. If the **length** of a wire is doubled, its **resistance** will double, but its **resistivity** will remain unchanged because it is a characteristic of the substance itself. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SI Unit and Symbol:**

 
 
• The **SI unit** of **resistivity** is the **Ohm-meter (Ω⋅m)**.
 
• It is represented by the Greek letter **ρ (rho)**.
 
 
 
• **Classification of Materials:**
 
 
• **Conductors:** Materials like **Silver** and **Copper** have very low **resistivity**, typically in the range of **10^-8 Ω⋅m**. **Silver** is known to have the lowest **resistivity** (approx **1.59 × 10^-8 Ω⋅m**) at **20°C**.
 
• **Insulators:** Materials like **Glass**, **Rubber**, and **Ebonite** have high **resistivity**, ranging from **10^12 to 10^17 Ω⋅m**.
 
• **Semiconductors:** Materials like **Silicon** and **Germanium** have **resistivity** levels between those of **conductors** and **insulators**.
 
 
 
• **Temperature Effect:**
 
 
• For **metals**, **resistivity** generally increases with an increase in **temperature** because thermal vibrations of atoms interfere with the flow of **electrons**.
 
• For **semiconductors** and **insulators**, **resistivity** usually decreases as **temperature** increases because more **charge carriers** become available for conduction.
 
 
 
• **Alloys:**
 
 
• The **resistivity** of an **alloy** (like **Constantan** or **Manganin**) is generally higher than that of its constituent **metals**.
 
• **Alloys** do not oxidize (burn) readily at high temperatures, which is why they are used in **electrical heating devices** like **toasters** and **electric irons**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The distinction between **resistance** and **resistivity** is crucial: **Resistance** is a property of the specific object (depending on **size** and **shape**), whereas **resistivity** is a property of the **substance**.
 
• In the **year 1827**, **Georg Simon Ohm** published his discovery of the relationship between **current**, **voltage**, and **resistance**, which eventually led to the definition of **resistivity**.
 
• Factors affecting **Resistance**: **Length**, **Area of cross-section**, **Nature of material**, and **Temperature**.
 
• Factors affecting **Resistivity**: Only **Nature of material** and **Temperature**.

questions.question: The image formed by a convex mirror is always _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**virtual and erect**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **convex mirror**, also known as a **diverging mirror**, is a curved mirror in which the reflective surface bulges toward the light source. It always forms an image that is **virtual**, **erect**, and **diminished** (smaller than the object), regardless of the distance between the object and the mirror.
 
• **Statement A (Real and erect)**: In optics, **real images** are typically formed by the actual convergence of light rays and are almost always **inverted**. A single mirror cannot produce an image that is simultaneously real and erect for a real object. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

• **Comparison with Concave Mirror**: Unlike a convex mirror, a **concave mirror** can form **real**, **inverted**, **virtual**, **erect**, **magnified**, or **diminished** images depending on the **location** of the object relative to the **center of curvature (C)** and **focus (F)**.

questions.question: Which of the following natural phenomena CANNOT be explained by the Universal Law of Gravitation?

options.text: Revolution of the Moon around the Earth
Falling of an apple from a tree

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Attraction between magnets**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Universal Law of Gravitation**, formulated by **Sir Isaac Newton** in **1687**, states that every particle of matter in the universe attracts every other particle with a force that is directly proportional to the product of their **masses** and inversely proportional to the square of the **distance** between them.
 
• **Tides in the ocean** are primarily caused by the **gravitational pull** of the **Moon** and the **Sun** acting on the **Earth's** water bodies. As the **Earth** rotates, this pull creates the periodic rise and fall of sea levels. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct (it is explained by gravitation).***
 
• **Attraction between magnets** is a phenomenon governed by the **electromagnetic force**, specifically **magnetic fields** generated by moving **electric charges** or **intrinsic magnetic moments** of electrons. While magnets have **mass** and exert a negligible gravitational pull on each other, the force that causes them to snap together is not **gravity**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect (it cannot be explained by gravitation).***
 
• The **revolution of the Moon around the Earth** is maintained by the **gravitational force** of the **Earth**, which provides the necessary **centripetal force** to keep the **Moon** in its nearly circular **orbit**. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct (it is explained by gravitation).***
 
• The **falling of an apple from a tree** toward the ground is the classic example used to describe **Earth's gravity**. The **Earth** exerts an attractive force on the **mass** of the apple, causing it to accelerate at approximately **9.8 m/s²**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct (it is explained by gravitation).***

__
 
• **Fundamental Forces of Nature:**

 
 
• There are **four fundamental forces**: **Gravitational Force**, **Electromagnetic Force**, **Strong Nuclear Force**, and **Weak Nuclear Force**.
 
• **Gravitational Force** is the weakest of the four but has an **infinite range** and is always **attractive**.
 
• **Electromagnetic Force** acts between **charged particles** and can be either **attractive or repulsive**. It is significantly stronger than **gravity** at small scales.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Principia Mathematica:**
 
 
• **Newton** published his findings in the **Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica** in **July 1687**, which laid the foundations for **classical mechanics**.

• **Universal Gravitational Constant (G):**
 
 
• The value of **G** was first accurately measured by **Henry Cavendish** in **1798** using a **torsion balance**.
 
• The modern accepted value is approximately **6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N⋅m²/kg²**.

• **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity**, which varies depending on the **location** (e.g., it is different on the **Moon** compared to **Earth**).
 
 
 
• **Inverse Square Law:**
 
 
• Because the force is **inversely proportional** to the **square of the distance**, doubling the distance between two objects reduces the **gravitational pull** to **one-fourth** of its original strength.
 
 
 
• **Centripetal Force in Orbits:**
 
 
• In the case of **satellites** or **planets**, the **gravitational force** acts as the **centripetal force**, which is required for **curved motion**. Without this force, objects would move in a **straight line** due to **inertia**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about epithelial tissue is correct?

options.text: Epithelial tissue forms a protective covering and regulates material exchange.
Epithelial tissue cells have large intercellular spaces and form a loose sheet.
Epithelial tissue does not play any role in material exchange in the body.
Epithelial tissue mainly connects bones and muscles.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Epithelial tissue forms a protective covering and regulates material exchange**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Epithelial tissue** is a primary tissue type that covers the **external surfaces** of the body and lines **internal organs** and cavities. Its primary role is to act as a barrier and provide **protection** against mechanical injury, pathogens, and dehydration. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The cells in epithelial tissue are **tightly packed** and form a continuous sheet. They have an extremely small amount of **cementing material** between them and almost no **intercellular spaces**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• This tissue is crucial for **regulating the exchange of materials** between the body and the external environment, as well as between different parts of the body. The **permeability** of the epithelial cells allows for the controlled movement of substances. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• Epithelial tissue is always separated from the underlying tissue by an extracellular fibrous **basement membrane**, which provides structural support.
 
• The function of connecting **bones and muscles** is performed by **Connective tissue** (specifically **tendons**), not by epithelial tissue. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Epithelial tissue forms a protective covering and regulates material exchange.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classification Based on Structure:**

 
 
• **Simple Squamous Epithelium:** These are **extremely thin** and flat cells forming a delicate lining. They are found in the **lung alveoli** and **blood vessels** where transport of substances occurs through a selective permeable surface.
 
• **Stratified Squamous Epithelium:** Found in the **skin**, these cells are arranged in many layers to prevent wear and tear.
 
• **Columnar Epithelium:** These are "pillar-like" cells found where **absorption and secretion** occur, such as the **inner lining of the intestine**.
 
• **Cuboidal Epithelium:** These cube-shaped cells provide **mechanical support** and are found in the lining of **kidney tubules** and ducts of **salivary glands**.
 
 
 
• **Specialized Epithelial Tissues:**
 
 
• **Ciliated Epithelium:** In the **respiratory tract**, columnar epithelial tissue has **cilia** (hair-like projections) that move to push mucus forward to clear it.
 
• **Glandular Epithelium:** Sometimes a portion of the epithelial tissue folds inward to form a **multicellular gland**, which secretes substances at the epithelial surface.
 
 
 
• **Functions:**
 
 
• **Protection:** Acts as the first line of defense (e.g., **skin**).
 
• **Absorption:** Absorbs nutrients in the **digestive tract**.
 
• **Secretion:** Secretes hormones, sweat, and enzymes through **glandular cells**.
 
• **Excretion:** Helps in the elimination of waste products in the **kidneys**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Characteristics:** Epithelial tissues are **avascular**, meaning they do not have their own blood supply; they receive nutrients via diffusion from the underlying connective tissue.
 
• **Location Examples:** It covers the **skin**, the lining of the **mouth**, the lining of **blood vessels**, **lung alveoli**, and **kidney tubules**.
 
• **Regeneration:** Epithelial cells have a high **regeneration capacity**, which is essential for surfaces that undergo frequent environmental stress or friction.

questions.question: A car is moving at a speed of 180 km/h. After the brakes are applied, it comes to a complete stop in 5 seconds. If the total mass of the car along with its passengers is 4200 kg, what is the force applied by the brakes to stop the car?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**–42,000 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The calculation of force is based on **Newton's Second Law of Motion**, which states that **Force (F) = mass (m) × acceleration (a)**.
 
• First, we must convert the **initial velocity (u)** of the car from **km/h** to **m/s** to maintain **SI unit** consistency. Given the speed is **180 km/h**, we multiply by **5/18**. Therefore, **u = 180 × (5/18) = 50 m/s**.
 
• The car comes to a **complete stop**, which means the **final velocity (v)** is **0 m/s**. The **time (t)** taken for this change is **5 seconds**.
 
• We calculate the **acceleration (a)** using the first equation of motion: **v = u + at**. Rearranging for **a**, we get **a = (v - u) / t**. Plugging in the values: **a = (0 - 50) / 5 = -10 m/s²**. ***Hence, the acceleration is –10 m/s².***
 
• The total **mass (m)** of the system (car + passengers) is **4200 kg**. Using the force formula: **F = 4200 kg × (-10 m/s²) = -42,000 N**.
 
• The **negative sign** in the result **–42,000 N** signifies that the force is acting in the **opposite direction** to the motion of the car, which is characteristic of a **braking or retarding force**. ***Hence, the correct answer is –42,000 N.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion**: This law provides a quantitative measure of force. It establishes that the **net force** acting on an object is equal to the rate of change of its **linear momentum**. For an object with a constant mass, it simplifies to the product of **mass** and **acceleration**.
 
• **Unit Conversion**: In physics problems, it is crucial to use the **International System of Units (SI)**. Velocity should be in **meters per second (m/s)**, mass in **kilograms (kg)**, and time in **seconds (s)**. The conversion factor **5/18** is derived from **1000 meters / 3600 seconds**.
 
• **Concept of Retardation**: When the velocity of an object decreases over time, the acceleration is negative. This is specifically referred to as **retardation** or **deceleration**. In this context, the brakes provide the necessary **frictional force** to cause this retardation.
 
• **The Newton (N)**: The SI unit of force is the **Newton**, named after **Sir Isaac Newton**. **1 Newton** is defined as the amount of force required to accelerate a **1 kg** mass at a rate of **1 m/s²**.
 
• **Applications**: Understanding braking force is essential in **automotive engineering** and **road safety**. It helps in determining **stopping distances** and designing efficient **braking systems** like **ABS (Anti-lock Braking System)** to handle large **inertial loads**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Momentum**: The **initial momentum** of the car was **4200 kg × 50 m/s = 210,000 kg·m/s**. The **final momentum** is **0**. The **impulse** provided by the brakes is equal to this change in momentum.
 
• **Force Direction**: Since force is a **vector quantity**, the sign is vital. A positive force would imply the car is speeding up, while the **negative force** confirms the application of brakes to reduce speed.
 
• **Mass Sensitivity**: If the **mass** of the car were lower, the same **braking force** would stop the car in **less time** or a **shorter distance**, demonstrating the role of **inertia** in motion.

questions.question: The absolute refractive index of a medium is defined as the ratio of ___________.

options.text: speed of light in vacuum to speed of light in medium
speed of light in water to speed of light in medium
speed of light in glass to speed of light in water
speed of light in medium to speed of light in vacuum

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**speed of light in vacuum to speed of light in medium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **absolute refractive index** of a medium is defined as the ratio of the **speed of light in a vacuum** to the **speed of light in the medium**.
 
• **Mathematically:** Refractive index (n) = c/v, where **c** is the speed of light in vacuum (approximately 3 × 10⁸ m/s) and **v** is the speed of light in the given medium.
 
• This property is a measure of how much the speed of light is reduced in a particular medium compared to a vacuum.
 
• The refractive index is dimensionless and always greater than or equal to 1, as light travels fastest in a vacuum.
 
• The refractive index affects phenomena like **refraction**, where light bends when transitioning between mediums of different refractive indices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speed of Light in Different Media:**

 
 
• In **vacuum**, the speed of light is approximately **3 × 10⁸ m/s**.
 
• In **air**, the speed of light is slightly less than in a vacuum but is often approximated as the same for practical purposes.
 
• In **water**, the speed of light is approximately **2.25 × 10⁸ m/s**, giving water a refractive index of about 1.33.
 
• In **glass**, the speed of light is around **2 × 10⁸ m/s**, with a refractive index of approximately 1.5.
 
 
 
• **Key Terminology:**
 
 
• **Vacuum:** A space devoid of matter where light travels at its maximum speed.
 
• **Medium:** A material (e.g., air, water, glass) through which light propagates.
 
• **Refractive Index:** A measure of how much light slows down and bends when entering a medium from a vacuum or another medium.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Refractive Index:**
 
 
• Used in designing optical devices such as **lenses** and **prisms**.
 
• Important in **fiber optic technology** for data transmission.
 
• Helps in studying the **composition of materials** and their optical properties.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts:**
 
 
• The refractive index of diamond is around **2.42**, making it highly effective in bending light and contributing to its brilliance.
 
• Refractive index is also used in **measuring the purity of substances**, such as liquids in industries.

questions.question: Which of the following factors does NOT increase the rate of evaporation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Increase in humidity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Evaporation** is the process in which liquid water transforms into water vapor due to the application of heat or environmental factors like wind speed and temperature.
 
• **Humidity** refers to the amount of water vapor present in the air. An increase in humidity reduces the capacity of air to absorb more water vapor, thereby **decreasing the rate of evaporation**.
 
• **Wind Speed:** An increase in wind speed enhances evaporation by carrying away the water vapor formed on the surface, allowing more liquid to evaporate. *Hence, this increases evaporation.*
 
• **Temperature:** Higher temperatures provide more energy to water molecules, increasing their movement and facilitating evaporation. *Hence, this increases evaporation.*
 
• **Surface Area:** A larger surface area exposes more molecules to the air, thus speeding up evaporation. *Hence, this increases evaporation.*
 
• **Humidity:** When humidity increases, the air becomes saturated with water vapor, thereby slowing down or halting evaporation altogether. *Hence, this factor does NOT increase evaporation.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors Affecting Evaporation:**

 
 
• **Temperature:** Higher temperatures increase the kinetic energy of water molecules, facilitating evaporation.
 
• **Wind Speed:** Wind helps disperse water vapor from the surface, making room for more liquid to evaporate.
 
• **Surface Area:** The larger the exposed surface area, the quicker the evaporation rate.
 
• **Humidity:** High humidity slows down evaporation as the air is already saturated with water vapor.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Evaporation:**
 
 
• **Drying Clothes:** Evaporation aids in the drying process by removing water molecules from the fabric.
 
• **Cooling Effect:** Sweating and the evaporation of sweat help regulate body temperature.
 
• **Industrial Uses:** Evaporation is used in industries for processes like salt production from seawater and concentrating solutions.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Principles:**
 
 
• **Latent Heat:** During evaporation, water molecules absorb energy, leading to a cooling effect.
 
• **Saturation Point:** When air reaches its saturation point, evaporation slows down or stops.
 
 
 
• **Examples in Nature:**
 
 
• **Water Cycle:** Evaporation plays a key role in the water cycle by converting water from oceans, rivers, and lakes into vapor.
 
• **Transpiration:** Plants lose water through evaporation from their leaves, which is essential for nutrient transport and temperature regulation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Humidity Measurement:** Humidity is measured using instruments like hygrometers and psychrometers. Meteorological departments track humidity levels to forecast weather conditions.
 
• **Evaporation in Daily Life:** Evaporation is observed in common activities such as boiling water, drying wet surfaces, and sweat evaporation.
 
• **Rate of Evaporation:** The rate can be influenced by environmental conditions, including temperature and wind speed.
 
• **Role in Cooling Systems:** Evaporation is utilized in cooling systems like air conditioners and cooling towers to dissipate heat.

questions.question: Galvanisation protects iron from rusting by coating it with a thin layer of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zinc metal only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Galvanisation** is a metallurgical process used to protect **Iron** and **Steel** from **Rusting** by applying a thin, protective coating of **Zinc**.
 
• The process is highly effective because **Zinc** acts as a physical barrier between the metal and the atmosphere, preventing **Oxygen** and **Moisture** from reaching the surface of the **Iron**.
 
• The most common method utilized in industries is **Hot-dip galvanizing**, where the metal components are submerged in a bath of molten **Zinc** at temperatures typically around **450 degrees Celsius** (**842 degrees Fahrenheit**).
 
• A unique feature of this process is **Sacrificial Protection**; since **Zinc** is more chemically active (electropositive) than **Iron**, it corrodes in preference to the **Iron**, even if the coating is scratched or damaged.
 
• While other metals like **Nickel**, **Chromium**, or **Tin** can be used for coating (in processes like electroplating), the specific term **Galvanisation** refers exclusively to the application of **Zinc**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rusting of Iron**:

 
 
• **Rusting** is an oxidation reaction that occurs when **Iron** reacts with **Oxygen** in the presence of **Water** or **Moisture**.
 
• The chemical formula for rust is **Fe2O3.nH2O**, which is known as **Hydrated Iron(III) Oxide**. It is a reddish-brown flaky substance that weakens the structural integrity of the metal.
 
 
 
• **Other Methods of Rust Prevention**:
 
 
• **Painting and Greasing**: Provides a simple barrier to block **Air** and **Water**.
 
• **Alloying**: Mixing **Iron** with elements like **Chromium** (at least **10.5%**) and **Nickel** produces **Stainless Steel**, which is highly resistant to corrosion.
 
• **Anodizing**: Primarily used for **Aluminium**, it thickens the natural oxide layer on the metal surface.
 
• **Tinning**: Coating **Iron** or **Steel** with **Tin**, often used for food containers as **Tin** is non-toxic.
 
 
 
• **Comparison of Options**:
 
 
• **Silver**: It is an expensive precious metal and would be economically unviable for industrial rust protection.
 
• **Copper**: If used as a coating, it can actually accelerate the corrosion of **Iron** if the coating is breached because **Iron** is more reactive than **Copper**.
 
• **Nickel**: Used in **Electroplating** to provide a shiny finish and corrosion resistance, but it does not provide the same sacrificial protection as **Zinc**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term **Galvanisation** is named after the **Italian** scientist **Luigi Galvani**, who studied the effects of electricity on biological tissues, though the industrial coating process was developed later in the **19th Century**.
 
• In a **Galvanic Cell** setup, the **Zinc** acts as the **Anode** and the **Iron** acts as the **Cathode**, ensuring the base metal remains protected as long as the **Zinc** is present.
 
• Common applications of galvanized **Iron** include **Roofing sheets**, **Water pipes**, **Fencing**, and **Automotive body parts**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a neutralisation reaction?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **neutralisation reaction** is a chemical reaction in which an **acid** and a **base** react quantitatively with each other to form **water** and a **salt**.
 
• The reaction **NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O** involves **Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH)**, which is a **strong base**, and **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl)**, which is a **strong acid**. They react to produce **Sodium Chloride (NaCl)**, a neutral salt, and **water (H₂O)**. ***Hence, the statement representing this reaction is correct.***
 
• In the reaction **Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu**, **Iron (Fe)** displaces **Copper (Cu)** from the **Copper Sulphate** solution because iron is more reactive. This is a **single displacement reaction**, not neutralisation. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The reaction **CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂** represents the **thermal decomposition** of **Calcium Carbonate** into **Calcium Oxide** and **Carbon Dioxide** upon heating. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• In the reaction **Zn + HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂**, **Zinc (Zn)** reacts with **Hydrochloric Acid** to produce **Zinc Chloride** and **Hydrogen gas**. This is another example of a **displacement reaction**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nature of Neutralisation:**

 
 
• Neutralisation reactions are generally **exothermic** in nature, meaning they release **heat energy** during the process.
 
• The **heat of neutralisation** is the change in **enthalpy** when one equivalent of an acid is neutralised by one equivalent of a base.
 
 
 
• **pH Scale and Indicators:**
 
 
• In a complete neutralisation of a strong acid and a strong base, the resulting solution has a **pH value** of **7** at **25 degrees Celsius**.
 
• **Phenolphthalein** is a common **indicator** used in these reactions; it turns **pink** in basic solutions and becomes **colourless** when the solution is neutralised or acidic.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• **Antacids:** **Magnesium Hydroxide**, commonly known as **Milk of Magnesia**, is used to neutralise excess **hydrochloric acid** in the stomach to treat **acidity**.
 
• **Soil Treatment:** If the **soil** is too acidic, farmers add **Quick Lime (Calcium Oxide)** or **Slaked Lime (Calcium Hydroxide)** to neutralise it for better crop growth.
 
• **Insect Stings:** The effect of an **ant sting**, which contains **methanoic acid (formic acid)**, can be neutralised by rubbing **moist baking soda (Sodium Hydrogen Carbonate)** or **calamine solution**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Types of Salts Formed:**

 
 
• A **strong acid** reacting with a **strong base** produces a **neutral salt** (e.g., **NaCl**).
 
• A **strong acid** reacting with a **weak base** produces an **acidic salt** (e.g., **Ammonium Chloride**).
 
• A **weak acid** reacting with a **strong base** produces a **basic salt** (e.g., **Sodium Acetate**).
 
 
 
• **Arrhenius Theory:** According to the **Arrhenius definition**, an **acid** provides **Hydrogen ions (H+)** and a **base** provides **Hydroxide ions (OH-)** in aqueous solutions. During neutralisation, these ions combine to form **water (H₂O)**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a part of the central nervous system in human?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Spinal cord** is a vital part of the **Central Nervous System (CNS)**, which consists of the brain and spinal cord. It serves as the primary communication highway between the brain and the rest of the body.
 
• The CNS is responsible for processing, interpreting, and responding to sensory inputs, motor outputs, and cognitive functions. The spinal cord plays a critical role in transmitting **nerve signals** to and from the brain.
 
• The spinal cord is protected by the vertebral column and is encased in meninges, which are layers of connective tissue that ensure safety and nourishment.
 
• It consists of **white matter** (nerve fibers) and **grey matter** (nerve cell bodies). The spinal cord enables reflex actions, which are quick responses to stimuli without involving the brain.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about the magnetic field inside a solenoid?

options.text: It is uniform and in the form of parallel straight lines.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is uniform and in the form of parallel straight lines**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The magnetic field inside a solenoid is **uniform** and consists of **parallel straight lines**, which indicates that the field strength and direction are consistent throughout the solenoid.
 
• A solenoid is essentially a coil of wire wound in a cylindrical form, and when an electric current flows through it, it generates a **magnetic field** along its axis.
 
• The uniformity of the field inside the solenoid occurs due to the **symmetrical arrangement** of the current-carrying loops and the resulting superposition of their individual magnetic fields.
 
• This uniform magnetic field is crucial in applications such as **electromagnets**, **magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)**, and various types of sensors and actuators.
 
• The strength of the magnetic field inside the solenoid can be calculated using the formula: **B = μ₀ × n × I**, where **μ₀** is the permeability of free space, **n** is the number of turns per unit length, and **I** is the current flowing through the solenoid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Magnetic Field Inside a Solenoid:**

 
 
• The field is strong and uniform, making it ideal for scientific and industrial applications.
 
• Outside the solenoid, the magnetic field is significantly weaker compared to the inside.
 
• The direction of the magnetic field inside the solenoid follows the **right-hand rule**, where the direction of curled fingers represents the current, and the thumb represents the field direction.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Solenoids:**
 
 
• Used in **electromagnets** to lift heavy objects in industrial settings.
 
• Essential in **electric relays** and **valves** for controlling mechanical operations.
 
• Utilized in **medical imaging technologies** such as MRI machines.
 
• In scientific experiments, solenoids provide controlled magnetic fields for studying various phenomena.
 
 
 
• **Other Magnetic Field Patterns:**
 
 
• **Non-uniform fields:** These occur in irregular arrangements of current-carrying conductors.
 
• **Zero field:** Found in areas where no current flows or magnetic effects cancel out.
 
• **Random patterns:** Observed in disorganized setups without symmetry.
 
 
 
• **Important Formula:**
 
 
• The strength of the magnetic field inside a solenoid is given by: **B = μ₀ × n × I**, where:
 
 
• **μ₀**: Permeability of free space (4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A).
 
• **n**: Number of turns per unit length.
 
• **I**: Current in amperes.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Solenoid Design:**

 
 
• Solenoids are typically constructed using insulated copper wire wound around a cylindrical core.
 
• The core can be made of air, iron, or other ferromagnetic materials to enhance field strength.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Magnetic Field Uniformity:**
 
 
• Uniform fields are highly useful in **particle accelerators** and **plasma confinement** devices.
 
• Such fields are also exploited in designing **linear motors** and **induction coils**.

• Vegetative propagation is widely used in **horticulture and agriculture** for commercial cultivation of high-yield or disease-resistant varieties.

questions.question: Where is the embryo implanted after fertilisation in the human female body under normal conditions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uterus lining**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After fertilization, the **zygote travels through the oviduct (fallopian tube)** towards the uterus.
 
• By the time it reaches the uterus, the zygote has developed into a structure called a **blastocyst**.
 
• The **uterus lining**, also known as the **endometrium**, is prepared during the menstrual cycle to receive and nourish the blastocyst. **It thickens and becomes rich in blood vessels under the influence of hormones like estrogen and progesterone.**
 
• **Implantation** occurs in the uterus lining, where the blastocyst attaches itself and begins to grow, forming a connection with the mother’s blood supply.
 
• The **endometrium** provides all the necessary nutrients and support to the developing embryo during the early stages of pregnancy.
 
• Other structures like the **oviduct, ovary,** and **cervix** do not play a role in implantation. These structures serve different functions in the reproductive process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Oviduct (Fallopian Tube):**

 
 
• The oviduct is the site of **fertilization**, where the sperm meets the egg.
 
• It plays no role in implantation but helps transport the fertilized egg (zygote) to the uterus.
 
• Blockage or dysfunction in the oviduct can lead to complications such as **ectopic pregnancy**, where the embryo implants outside the uterus.
 
 
 
• **Ovary:**
 
 
• The ovaries produce **ova (eggs)**, which are necessary for reproduction.
 
• They also produce hormones like **estrogen and progesterone** that regulate the menstrual cycle and prepare the uterus for potential pregnancy.
 
• However, the ovary does not contribute to the implantation process.
 
 
 
• **Cervix:**
 
 
• The cervix is the lower part of the uterus that opens into the vagina.
 
• It serves as a passage for sperm to travel to the uterus and for menstrual blood to exit the body.
 
• The cervix does not play any direct role in the process of implantation.
 
 
 
• **Endometrium:**
 
 
• The endometrium undergoes cyclic changes during the menstrual cycle to prepare for potential implantation.
 
• If implantation does not occur, the endometrium is shed during menstruation.
 
• If implantation occurs, the endometrium provides the growing embryo with nutrients and support until the placenta forms.
 
 
 
• **Hormonal Regulation:**
 
 
• Hormones like **estrogen** and **progesterone** are essential for preparing the endometrium for implantation.
 
• These hormones are primarily produced by the corpus luteum in the ovary during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle.
 
• After implantation, the developing embryo secretes **human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)**, which helps maintain the corpus luteum and continued progesterone production.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Conditions for Successful Implantation:**

 
 
• A healthy and receptive uterus lining is crucial for successful implantation.
 
• Hormonal imbalances, infections, or structural abnormalities in the uterus can hinder implantation.
 
 
 
• **Ectopic Pregnancy:**
 
 
• If implantation occurs outside the uterus, such as in the oviduct, it leads to a condition called **ectopic pregnancy**.
 
• This is a medical emergency that requires immediate attention.
 
 
 
• **Role of Placenta:**
 
 
• After implantation, the placenta begins to form and takes over the role of providing nutrients and oxygen to the growing fetus.
 
• The placenta also removes waste products and produces hormones to sustain pregnancy.

questions.question: What property distinguishes a compound from a mixture?

options.text: There is a fixed balance and characteristics

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**There is a fixed balance and characteristics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **compound** is a substance formed when two or more chemical elements are **chemically bonded** together. The most defining characteristic of a compound is that the elements are always present in **fixed ratios** by mass.
 
• This fixed ratio is governed by the **Law of Definite Proportions** (also known as **Proust's Law**), which states that a chemical compound always contains its component elements in a fixed ratio and does not depend on its source or method of preparation.
 
• Unlike mixtures, the formation of a compound involves a **chemical change**, resulting in a product with **entirely different properties** from its constituent elements. For example, **Sodium** (a reactive metal) and **Chlorine** (a toxic gas) combine to form **Sodium Chloride** (common table salt).
 
• Compounds possess a **fixed melting and boiling point**, which serves as a benchmark for their **purity**. Because they are held together by chemical bonds (ionic or covalent), they cannot be separated by simple **physical methods** like filtration or evaporation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mixtures**:

 
 
• Components are physically combined and can be present in **any proportion**.
 
• They retain the **original properties** of their constituents (e.g., in a mixture of iron and sulfur, iron remains magnetic).
 
• They can be **homogeneous** (uniform composition like **Alloys**) or **heterogeneous** (non-uniform like **Soil**).
 
• Separation is possible through **physical processes** such as **distillation**, **sublimation**, or **magnetism**.
 
 
 
• **Separation of Compounds**:
 
 
• Compounds can only be broken down into their individual elements through **chemical reactions** or **electrochemical reactions** like **electrolysis**.
 
 
 
• **States of Matter**:
 
 
• The option **Always solid** is incorrect because compounds can exist in all three states of matter: **solid** (Calcium Carbonate), **liquid** (Water), and **gas** (Carbon Dioxide).
